card: Adds a TxCollection mining IPC interface that allows external services, such as Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers (JDS), to assemble and validate candidate block templates from a list of WTXIDs without transmitting known transactions over IPC. External template coordinators currently face high bandwidth and memory overhead synchronizing mempool mirrors or serializing entire blocks across process boundaries. The interface resolves WTXIDs against the node mempool, accepts missing transaction payloads, and validates the assembled block against the chain tip using TestBlockValidity. This work enables bandwidth-efficient custom template validation for Stratum v2, demonstrated in sv2-apps PR #599.
changed_since_previous: No substantial architectural changes; commits were rebased onto recent mining interface and template manager changes.
evidence: PR description: "We build and validate the block template ourselves now, based on the requested transaction list and our own mempool, so known transactions don't need to cross the IPC boundary. This also fits the draft spec for JDS custom job validation through a Template Provider."
Demonstrated integration in Stratum v2 reference implementation: https://github.com/stratum-mining/sv2-apps/pull/599
problem: External mining services that validate custom miner templates, such as Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers (JDS), need to verify blocks against the node's chain tip. Currently, they either must mirror the entire mempool in their own process or transfer every full transaction across the IPC boundary, causing high memory and IPC bandwidth overhead.

risk.why: Flaws in template assembly, coinbase generation refactoring, or validation checks could cause mining coordinators to approve invalid blocks or reject valid miner templates.

scope_notes: Modifies Cap'n Proto IPC definitions in src/ipc/capnp/mining.capnp and refactors coinbase construction in src/node/miner.cpp alongside adding new node mining interfaces and tests.
summary: Adds the TxCollection interface and Cap'n Proto IPC methods to assemble and validate block templates from an ordered list of witness transaction IDs (WTXIDs). Matches requested WTXIDs against the node's local mempool, reports missing transaction positions to the client, ingests missing transaction payloads, and validates the completed block against the active tip using TestBlockValidity. Also refactors coinbase construction in BlockAssembler into a reusable helper so candidate blocks can be validated against either a node-generated dummy coinbase or a client-supplied coinbase.
